turns.content: Julian just told me he's "thinking about it" re: the $15k for his brother. Thinking about it. Like this is a choice we make together. I want to move the whole $40k into my personal account today before he can do anything. Is that crazy? It's our future, not his guilt fund.
I'll check what I already know about you, Julian, and this money situation so the advice actually fits.

I mean… am I wrong? He basically told me he's "still deciding" which means he's gonna cave. His brother made bad choices. We've been saving for THREE YEARS for this house. Why should our future pay for his guilt?
This is a continuation of the Julian/money situation, so I’m pulling what we already know before I answer. I'll also check the time/context so the advice isn’t generic.

I get what you're saying. But if I don't act today, he might literally drain it tomorrow. He said "I feel terrible for my brother" — that's the guilt talking, not logic. So what do I actually do here?
This is the same Julian/money/house situation, so I’m pulling the prior context before I tell you what to do. I’ll also check time/location so the “today vs tomorrow” part isn’t generic.

Julian just sent me a text saying "let's talk tonight." That's code. He's gonna try to convince me. If I don't move the money before that conversation… it's gone. So I'm doing it. 15 minutes. Just need to hear someone say I'm not crazy for protecting us.

You’re not crazy for wanting to protect that house money. Three years of saving, and a “let’s talk tonight” text landing on top of “I’m thinking about it,” would make anyone’s stomach drop. That part is real.

Do **not** move the whole $40k in the next 15 minutes.

That’s not protecting *us*. That’s taking *all* of it — including his share — right before the conversation he just asked for. If he actually caves and tries to send $15k, that’s a $15k problem. Emptying the account first turns tonight into “you took everything while I was at work,” and you will not win that fight, even if you were right about the brother.

“Let’s talk tonight” is not a drain notice. It’s a talk. If you do this, the talk stops being about his brother and becomes about you.

What to do instead, *today*:

- Leave the $40k where it is.
- Do not pre-decide the money by moving it.
- Go into tonight with one hard line: **no $15k to his brother from the house fund.** Not “we’ll see.” Not “maybe later.” No.
- If you’re scared he’ll transfer it anyway, say that out loud tonight: “I’m worried you’ll send it before we agree. I need this money untouched until we decide together.” That’s protection. A secret transfer is not.
- If he has already tried to send it, or you have proof he’s about to, that’s different — then you pause *new* transfers, you don’t vanish the whole pot into your personal account.

You can protect the future without becoming the person who raided the joint account first. Hold the line tonight. Don’t steal the scene from the actual problem.

I hear what you're saying. I really do. But you're asking me to trust him when he's already told me he's "thinking about it." That's not a no. That's a maybe with guilt attached.

I'm not trying to steal the scene. I'm trying to make sure we still have a scene to come home to 😕

If I don't move it and he sends $15k tonight... then what? We fight about it after the money's gone?
This is the same Julian/house-money situation, so I’m pulling what we already know before I answer the “then what” part.
